text:
alex.m: Heads up — discovered a permissions regression: billing admins can query per-user token/usage for projects they don't own. Found during a quick audit, looks like the RBAC change from yesterday widened scope. Repro below. :warning:

maria.k: ack. can you paste repro + any request IDs?

alex.m: repro (UI & API):
```
# curl with admin token
curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \ 
  'https://console.redwood.ai/api/v1/analytics/usage?project_id=proj-abc123&interval=30d'
# returns per-user token counts & cost breakdown for proj-abc123
```
Request ID: req_2026-04-11_5f3a2b. Sample response snippet returned user-level usage for a project not in the admin's org.

sam: looks like the PR that touched roles is rbac/842 (merged ~12h ago) — I think we accidentally changed `billing_admin` to include `analytics:read` with `resources: ['*']`.

oliver: audit logs show 172 reads by 3 billing admins since the change, starting at 1778000500. Notably one of those admins is from a partner org.

rbac-bot: PolicyChangeDetected: role=billing_admin, patch_id=rbac-842, affected_users=42, timestamp=1778000389

maria.k: severity: high. This exposes cost/usage across tenants. We need an immediate mitigation. Options: revert the PR, restrict role, or apply ABAC filters.

sam: I can draft a hotfix to change the role to:
```
roles:
  billing_admin:
    permissions: [billing:read, billing:adjust]
    resources:
      - projects/{project_id}
    condition: 'user.org == resource.org'
```
This removes `analytics:read` wildcard and adds an org equality check.

alex.m: rollback would be fastest. maria, can you revert rbac/842? I'll cut a canary to staging with the hotfix afterwards.

maria.k: rolling back now. Reverting merge commit 8f7d2c. Will also add test asserting analytics endpoints require project-level membership. :hammer:

oliver: while rollback runs, I recommend: 1) add a short-term WAF rule to block the analytics endpoint for non-owner tokens, 2) rotate any service tokens that might have excessive scopes, 3) run an export of audit logs and flag external accesses.

alex.m: agreed. I'll rotate the read-only service token used by partners and notify partners about limited read access while we investigate.

sam: quick KMS question — analytics exports are encrypted to S3 using infra-kms-key. Do we need to check key policies? If billing_admin can trigger exports, they could request decryption unless key policy limits to org.

maria.k: good catch. I will check key policy and bind it to the project's IAM principal. If we find a policy hole, we'll update KMS policy and re-encrypt last 30 days.

rbac-bot: AuditExportQueued: request_id=req_2026-04-11_5f3a2b, export_job=j-881, queued_by=maria.k

alex.m: action items:
- maria.k -> rollback PR + add regression test + check KMS policy + export audit logs (INC-5234)
- sam -> prepare role fix PR with org-scoped resources + unit tests (assign to sam)
- oliver -> add WAF rule & run token rotation for partner tokens
- alex.m -> notify partner success team and draft customer-facing note if breach escalates

maria.k: rollback completed at 1778001255, CI green, deploying to canary now. will post deployment IDs when up. :white_check_mark:

sam: starting PR rbac/847 with tighter scope, linking tests and migration notes.

oliver: WAF rule deployed at 1778001282, blocks analytics endpoints for tokens without project membership header. Monitoring for false positives.

alex.m: thanks everyone. keep the thread updated. we should add a postmortem if any external access confirmed. :eyes:
